thread:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (switch to kernel-v2 for shorter seq paths) we started seeing steady batch growth + padding waste on a subset of traces. Memory charts show a slow upward drift in per-GPU working set during continuous batching. Anyone else see this?

maria: I saw the alert. Repro steps: run a 30m replay with the new kernel and kv-cache enabled. I ran that locally and captured allocator slabs + workspace sizing. Short log:

```
ALLOC: slab_total=12.1G slab_used=9.3G workspace_reserved=1.8G pad_overhead=420M
BATCH: avg_batch_tokens=514 -> 614 over 20m
KV: entries_evicted=312 last_eviction_time=11:02:13
```

maria: The pad_overhead number climbed steadily after ~7m into the run.

jin: FYI the KV eviction spikes line up with a pattern I saw in tracing: kernel-v2 changes the tiled-kernel layout which nudges workspace allocations to different slab alignments, causing more small pad fragments. I have a small flamegraph diff but it's noisy.

sam: Can you paste the flame snippet? Also what was the allocator watermark before/after?

jin: snippet:
```
flame: workspace_alloc -> tiled_kernel_launch -> allocate_slab(64K) -> split -> pad_fragment -> retain
-- after change: more split()/retain() calls, avg fragment size ~6KB -> increases pad churn
```

maria: allocator watermark was 512MB per-stream before, we bumped to 768MB in the rollout to reduce frequent reclaims. Might be interacting.

alex: So two knobs: kernel layout changed allocation pattern, and watermark up means slabs stick around longer -> pad accumulates. Could explain the slow memory drift.

sam: Quick experiment suggestion: revert watermark to 512MB and run replay with kernel-v2 but force gc/eviction after each 50ms batch. If memory drift stops, it's the watermark interaction. If not, it's kernel padding.

perf-bot: nightly-continuous-batch:build-2027 reported +9% pad-allocs and +5% tail-latency on 50k replay. Full report: https://perf.internal/reports/2027 (attached).

maria: I ran a short A/B: kernel-v1+wm=768 vs kernel-v2+wm=512. Results: kernel-v2+wm=512 still had slightly higher pad waste than v1 (~+3%), but growth curve flattened. So both factors matter.

alex: Good. Action items: 1) jin to instrument split()/retain() path with per-seq counters (so we can attribute pad waste to seq length distribution), 2) sam to test auto-watermark that decays based on recent reclaim rate, 3) maria to run a longer 4h replay with kv eviction logging on.

sam: I'll sketch the auto-decay: watermark = max(min_wm, recent_reclaim_rate * factor). Quick patch posted to PR #3321.

jin: Added brief probe to runtime: `--alloc-pad-trace=1` logs per-seq pad bytes and caller-kernel. Will run tonight and upload CSV.

maria: Also noticed small perf regression in kernel-v2 on very short sequences (<8 tokens) — tail calls to tiled kernel add overhead that increases per-seq bookkeeping. Might be worth a micro-optimization to skip tiling for tiny sequences.

alex: OK let's coordinate: if jin's probe shows pad concentrated in mid-length sequences (64-256) we optimize tiling or allocator split heuristics. If it's short seqs, optimize kernel selection fallback. Ping me when probes are in. :thumbsup:

sam: filing a quick follow-up thread with experiment IDs and scripts.

perf-bot: experiment-ids: replay-2027-331 (v1), replay-2027-332 (v2, wm512), replay-2027-333 (v2, wm768). CSVs will land in s3://redwood-perf/2027/replays/

alex: Thanks all — priority-medium. We'll hold the rollout until we have a mitigation (auto-watermark or tiny-seq fast path).
